subsystems.name: Expansion Bay
subsystems.role: a standardized slot that accepts a graphics module, extra storage, or other high-bandwidth add-ons.

subsystems.name: Input Modules
subsystems.role: lets keyboards, numpads, and touchpads be swapped and repositioned by the user.

subsystems.name: Expansion Cards
subsystems.role: user-swappable I/O ports such as USB-C, USB-A, HDMI, or Ethernet.

subsystems.name: Mainboard
subsystems.role: core computing, memory, storage, and power delivery.

subsystems.name: Cooling System
subsystems.role: dissipates heat from the CPU and any swappable GPU module.

subsystems.name: Battery
subsystems.role: provides portable power and is itself replaceable.

buildSteps.title: Define modular interfaces
buildSteps.detail: Specify mechanical dimensions, electrical pinouts, and hot-swap protocols for every module so parts from different production runs fit together.

buildSteps.title: Manufacture chassis
buildSteps.detail: Precision-mill aluminum or magnesium alloy into the base and lid, with cutouts that accept the expansion bay and input modules.

buildSteps.title: Produce mainboard
buildSteps.detail: Assemble the CPU, memory, storage, and power circuitry on a printed circuit board, then flash firmware that recognizes hot-swapped modules.

buildSteps.title: Build individual modules
buildSteps.detail: Assemble keyboards, expansion cards, and the graphics module on separate lines, each tested for fit and electrical continuity.

buildSteps.title: Final assembly
buildSteps.detail: Combine chassis, mainboard, cooling, battery, and modules; install the operating system and configuration software.

buildSteps.title: Test and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Verify each module's function, hot-swap capability, and thermal performance under load.

buildSteps.title: Package and distribute
buildSteps.detail: Ship with documentation and tools that let users open, repair, and upgrade the laptop themselves.
